# drscl

> Scales a vector by the reciprocal of a scalar, performing the scaling.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import drscl from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/drscl';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
drscl( N, sa, x, strideX ) → Float64Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of elements |
| `sa` | `number` | Scalar divisor |
| `x` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | `x` stride length |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The number of components of the vector x.
- `sa`: The scalar a which is used to divide each component of x. `SA` must be \>= 0, or the subroutine will divide by zero.
- `x`: The n-element vector x.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: output array

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
drscl.ndarray( N, sa, x, strideX, offsetX ) → Float64Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of elements |
| `sa` | `number` | Scalar divisor |
| `x` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output array |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | Stride length for `x` |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `x` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The number of components of the vector x.
- `sa`: The scalar a which is used to divide each component of x. `SA` must be \>= 0, or the subroutine will divide by zero.
- `x`: The n-element vector x.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: input array

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `drscl()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DRSCL`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/drscl.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import drscl from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/drscl';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const x = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = drscl( N, 1, x, 1 );
console.log( out );

// Using the ndarray interface:
out = drscl.ndarray( N, 1, x, 1, 0 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DRSCL`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DRSCL multiplies an n-element real vector x by the real scalar 1/a. This is done without overflow or underflow as long as the final result x/a does not overflow or underflow.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
